previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex history including type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, gastroparesis, cirrhosis, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. He presented with lethargy and altered mental status, prompting a lumbar puncture which showed elevated protein but no infection, consistent with resolving toxic metabolic encephalopathy. Imaging revealed transient hydronephrosis in one transplanted kidney, which resolved with Foley catheter placement. His symptoms improved with supportive care, nausea control, and medication adjustments. He regained mental clarity, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up for repeat renal ultrasound and outpatient lab monitoring.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S.

INDICATION:  ___ with history of renal transfer presenting with abdominal pain
and chills with nausea and vomiting.  Evaluate for signs of rejection.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to renal ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Renal transplant kidney labeled #1 has normal renal morphology and measures
8.8 cm.  Specifically, the cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity,
pyramids are normal, there is no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is
normal.  There is no hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.71 to 0.82, are
minimally elevated indicated, and previously measured 0.69-0.82.  The main
renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke and
continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 56 cm per
second.  Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The transplant renal
vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

Renal transplant kidney labeled #2 has normal renal morphology and measures
10.5 cm.  Specifically, the cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity,
pyramids are normal, there is no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is
normal.  There is no hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.74 to 0.89,
indicative of mildly elevated resistive indices, previously 0.7-0.86.  The
main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke and
continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with an elevated peak systolic velocity
of up to 323 centimeters/second, previously 300 centimeters/second. 
Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The transplant renal vein is
patent and shows normal waveform.

Evaluation of the bladder demonstrates multiple hypoechoic lesions without
internal vascularity likely representing debris.

IMPRESSION:


1. Stable minimally elevated resistive indices of the superior right kidney
transplant, similar to prior exam.
2. Persistent increase in peak systolic velocity of the left main renal artery
of the inferior right kidney transplant measuring up to 223
centimeters/second, previously 300 centimeters/second.
3. Persistent minimally elevated resistive indices of the inferior renal
transplant, similar to prior exam.
4. Moderate bladder debris compared to prior exam.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ with history of cirrhosis presenting with abdominal pain. 
Evaluate for portal venous thrombosis or ascites

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to abdominal ultrasound performed ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears coarsened. The contour of the liver is
smooth. There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD measures 3 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
without masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic
tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN:  Normal echogenicity, measuring 8.9 cm.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the kidneys show no hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM:  The visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Main portal vein is patent.
2. Coarsened hepatic parenchyma, similar to prior exam.

EXAMINATION:  Chest radiograph

INDICATION:  ___ male with concern for free air in his mediastinum s/p
retching with hematemesis.  Evaluate for mediastinal air.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to chest radiograph dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Bilateral lungs are clear without evidence of focal consolidation.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax.  Moderate cardiomegaly is similar to prior exam. 
Leadless pacer generator device projecting over the left lower mid hemithorax
is similar to prior exam.  There is no radiographic evidence to suggest
pneumomediastinum.  Mild prominence of the pulmonary vasculature is similar to
prior exam and may be suggestive of a component of pulmonary vascular
congestion without frank pulmonary edema.

IMPRESSION: 

No radiographic evidence to suggest pneumomediastinum.  Otherwise no acute
intrathoracic process.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with nausea/vomiting/abdominal pain// Assess for
free air or signs of obstruction

TECHNIQUE:  Supine AP view of the abdomen

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis ___

FINDINGS: 

A nonspecific bowel gas pattern is demonstrated with a prominent loop of bowel
in the left upper abdomen, measuring up to 5.4 cm, which may be colonic in
origin.  Stool and gas are seen within the rectum.  Assessment for free
intraperitoneal air is limited on this supine view though no large amounts are
demonstrated.  Epicardial and pacing leads are seen projecting over the
midline lower chest and epigastric region.  No acute osseous abnormalities
seen.

IMPRESSION: 

Nonspecific bowel gas pattern.  If there is high concern for bowel
obstruction, recommend CT with intravenous and/or oral contrast for further
assessment.
